findings.description: Unsanitized 'directory' parameter is passed directly into an f-string used in os.system to construct a shell command. This allows command injection and arbitrary code execution, e.g., directory='; rm -rf /'. Also dangerous 'rm -rf' operation can cause data loss if directory paths are manipulated.

Unsanitized 'path' and 'host' parameters are interpolated into an f-string passed to subprocess.call with shell=True. This enables remote command execution through crafted values, e.g., path='--upload=none; malicious_command'. Additionally, hardcoded credentials and lack of input validation increase exposure.
execute_command directly passes user input to os.popen, executing arbitrary shell commands. This is a trivial remote code execution vector when input is attacker-controlled.

fix_description: Replace all shell-based execution with safe APIs: (1) For cleanup_old_files, use pathlib/shutil.rmtree on a resolved, validated directory path, never constructing a shell string. (2) For run_backup, use subprocess.run with a list of arguments (no shell=True) or better use a library like paramiko for SCP; validate host and path against strict patterns and avoid hardcoded credentials. (3) For execute_command, remove arbitrary command execution entirely; use a predefined whitelist of allowed commands and pass arguments as a list to subprocess.run without shell=True. Additionally, apply input validation, allowlisting, and least-privilege principles throughout.
